messages.content:
I searched for medical sources covering infant motor development, maternal self-care, breastfeeding milestones, and preparation for the 2-month pediatric visit, focusing on week 9 (approximately 2 months old).

**What I found:**

**Infant Motor Development (2 months):**
- CDC Developmental Milestones: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html (details movement/physical milestones like holding head up during tummy time)
- CDC Milestone Checklist: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/digital-online-checklist/2-months.html (interactive checklist for tracking progress)
- Parenting First Cry (9-week specifics): https://parenting.firstcry.com/articles/your-9-week-old-baby/ (notes typical weight gain of 1-1.5kg since birth)

**Maternal Self-Care Practices:**
- Geisinger Postpartum Self-Care: https://www.geisinger.org/patient-care/conditions-treatments-specialty/self-care-during-the-postpartum-period (recommends gentle exercise like walking for mood/energy)
- StatPearls Postpartum Care: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK565875/ (emphasizes comprehensive care including physical, emotional, social support and mental health)
- NCBI Postnatal Care Guidelines: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK304191/ (covers safety planning, home visits, family support)
- MedPark Hospital Postpartum Care: https://www.medparkhospital.com/en-US/lifestyles/postpartum-self-care (addresses breast engorgement management with compresses/pumping)
- Stanford Children's Health: https://www.stanfordchildrens.org/en/topic/default?id=the-new-mother-taking-care-of-yourself-after-birth-90-P02693 (advises daily outdoor time and postpartum exercises)

**Breastfeeding Milestones:**
- CDC Breastfeeding Guide: https://www.cdc.gov/infant-toddler-nutrition/breastfeeding/how-much-and-how-often.html (notes feeding frequency extends to every 2-4 hours as baby's stomach grows)
- KidsHealth Breastfeeding FAQ: https://kidshealth.org/en/parents/breastfeed-often.html (states 1-2 month olds typically nurse 7-9 times daily)
- Pampers Feeding Chart: https://www.pampers.com/en-us/baby/feeding/article/baby-feeding-schedule (indicates night feedings may reduce after birth weight regained ~2 weeks)
- Parents.com Feeding Guide: https://www.parents.com/baby/feeding/baby-feeding-chart-how-much-and-when-to-feed-infants-the-first-year/ (describes hunger cues and cautions crying is a late sign)
- La Leche League Frequency FAQ: https://llli.org/breastfeeding-info/frequency-feeding-frequently-asked-questions-faqs/ (explains wet/diaper stool outputs as nursing effectiveness indicators)

**Preparing for 2-Month Pediatric Visit:**
- The Bump 2-Month Checkup: https://www.thebump.com/a/babys-two-month-checkup (lists expected provider questions about feeding frequency, sleep patterns)
- MyHealthfinder Well-Visit Guide: https://odphp.health.gov/myhealthfinder/doctor-visits/regular-checkups/make-most-your-babys-visit-doctor-ages-0-11-months (notes discussions about parental well-being, baby's new skills, needed support)
- CDC Milestones in Action (2 months): https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones-in-action/2-months.html (visual examples of cognitive and movement milestones)

**Issues Encountered:**
The web_extract tool failed due to the current search-only backend (Brave Search). To extract full page content, the extraction backend would need to be configured to firecrawl, tavila, exa, or parallel. However, the web_search tool successfully provided relevant source URLs and descriptive snippets for all requested topics.

No files were created or modified during this research task. All sources are from authoritative medical, governmental, or reputable parenting organizations.
